frontier.hypothesis: H5'' -- target denies $a0 to neg_threshold via a PREFERENCE/conflict-graph effect that costs no instruction, not via an occupant of $a0.
frontier.mechanism: find_reg pass 0 excludes regs_someone_prefers[neg_threshold], which prune_preferences builds from LOWER-priority allocnos that CONFLICT with it and prefer $a0. Since a live occupant costs an instruction (measured: every occupant/hoist variant emits 108 vs 107), the original's conflict must come from conflict-graph construction rather than a real dynamic overlap -- e.g. global.c recording conflicts from a basic block's live-on-entry set, so an a0_var whose first set sits inside one reject arm conflicts with values live in the OTHER arm for free.
frontier.next_probe: Put a0_var's FIRST set inside one of the reject arms the chain branches to (the arms already exist and already store the return value, so a set there may cost nothing on the fall-through path); score with tmp/grind/func_8002EA24/s5/run.sh and read the chain registers off the dump. Then dump .lreg (cc1 ... -dl base.i) for the score-2 body and for plain1 and diff the quantity numbers of a0_var / x / neg_threshold to see whether local-alloc quantity merging is available as a lever. Verify any promising variant with tmp/grind/func_8002EA24/s3/findreg.sh 104 (someone_prefers / own_full_prefs) rather than by score alone.
